title: CURRENT TO CURSOR
territory: A substantial spoken current arriving at a quiet upright editing caret.
oneSentenceMeaning: A small movement of speech arrives beside a steady place to edit, turning everyday expression into something the speaker can keep shaping.
appIdentity: Mluva is open-source dictation and rewriting for Omarchy, named for the Czech word for speech or manner of speaking. Its everyday appeal is the ease of speaking a thought, seeing useful text appear, and continuing with the keyboard. The personality is calm, immediate and quietly delightful: a capable desktop companion that respects the user's attention. Original recognition, saved source and completed rewrites have separate identities; the editable result remains something the user can inspect and change, including exact Markdown. Speech and rewriting can use independently chosen local or cloud providers. The identity should express this practical freedom without suggesting that the product name guarantees local processing. Most delightful dictation for Omarchy is the creative ambition, and A little more delight every day is its human scale. This concept celebrates the handover into editable work rather than making a claim about recognition speed or accuracy.
markIdentity: Current to Cursor gives Mluva a mark built around a specific relationship: a short, substantial voiced form approaches an upright editing caret. The voice has a generous lower left origin and a single upward movement; the caret supplies a settled vertical rhythm. Their near meeting makes the image feel like language arriving somewhere useful. The voice is one filled body with no internal drawing, and the caret is a second solid shape. A visible interval preserves the distinction between source and editable result without attempting to diagram the application. Warmth comes from the voice body's uneven distribution of weight. Precision comes from its flat delivery edge and the straight receiver beside it. The mark should feel made for a keyboard fluent desktop while remaining approachable to someone who has never opened a terminal. Its signature is the blunt organic arrival against a still vertical, not a repeated oscillation or a piece of command syntax.
logoDescription:
The initial proposal is a horizontal pair of solid ink shapes, about one and a half times as wide as it is tall. At left, a compact voice current starts as a broad, low, rounded body and rises once toward a vertically cut end. At right, a tall caret waits across an open interval. The current occupies roughly three quarters of the visual mass, while the caret is lighter in area but longer in vertical reach. Both forms sit within one compact field; there is no containing square, circle or application tile.

Build the voice as a closed filled silhouette with independent upper and lower curves. Its lower left belly is the most generous part. The upper edge climbs toward a restrained shoulder at the right, while the lower edge lifts more decisively to meet the same delivery face. That difference creates pressure and direction without a pointed tip. The body should resemble one short spoken inflection compressed into a durable shape. Avoid a regular sine profile, repetitive humps or an audio meter. The current ends abruptly enough to establish a visual conversation with the upright beside it.

In this initial version, give the caret subtly softened corners and a width comparable to the current's narrowest section. Its top stands above the voice shoulder and its bottom reaches slightly below the belly. Leave enough space that neither form touches at thumbnail size. The empty interval matters: it lets the flowing material arrive without becoming a single fused glyph. The caret must remain an editing reference even when the source side reads only as a lively abstract mass.

Use one fully opaque dark ink, with every surrounding and internal empty area transparent. At large size, the asymmetry should reward looking without revealing a hidden illustration. At small size, the initial target is two clear masses with a low origin, an upper arrival and one steady vertical. This direction should bring a little warmth into Mluva's technical setting while providing a simple silhouette for a launcher, recorder header or repository signature. Its relationship to water is a quiet sense of movement and settling, not a literal wave scene.
wordmarkDescription:
The initial wordmark reads exactly Mluva, with one capital M and four lowercase letters. Start from JetBrains Mono Medium outlines, preserving the family connection to Mluva's editable interface and film typography. Treat the result as five carefully spaced letterforms rather than as a typed command. Keep the standard two-storey a, the clear open u and the recognizable diagonal construction of v. These familiar forms provide enough reading certainty to permit a few deliberate optical changes.

The main signature is the lowercase l. Narrow its body and advance so it becomes the word's quiet upright, recalling the mark's caret inside an actual letter. Retain a short upper flag and a restrained baseline foot to keep it distinguishable from a capital I or an accidental separator. Its vertical stem should feel firm and still, with nearly square terminals. The surrounding M and u should approach it through optical spacing, avoiding the conspicuous blank cell that an untouched monospaced l can create.

Give the u a slightly fuller lower left turn and a more controlled right return. This small distribution of curve weight echoes the voiced body without drawing a miniature symbol into the letter. Keep the v pointed enough to read immediately but ease the darkest interior junction. Open the a's counter slightly and finish its right stem with a clean vertical terminal. The M remains a confident anchor with two upright outer stems, clear internal diagonals and no stencil cuts.

The initial rhythm is compact, orderly and a little more supple than untouched code typography. Spacing between u and v can close optically, while the a retains sufficient breathing room around its bowl. Render the word as one ink color using filled letter shapes only. There is no extra caret, underscore, bracket, dot, prefix or icon. Distinction should come from the l's upright character, the u's quiet fullness and the overall pace of the five letters.
selfCritique: The initial wide arrangement risks becoming a waveform followed by a pipe character. If the viewer mentally types the symbol as approximate command syntax, the design has failed. The final mark needs a denser voice mass, a shorter horizontal journey and no repeated or recognizable punctuation contour.

A rising body with a swollen origin could resemble a musical note, a sperm shape or a sports swoosh. A small round head, a long thin neck or a sharp exit would strengthen those readings. Keep the whole body broad and blunt, with no bead, stalk or pointed tail.

An overly pill-shaped caret looks like a pause control or decorative exclamation stem. The receiver should be a nearly square-ended upright with moderate weight. Its distinct height and the single organic neighbor must carry the editing association without a second bar or a dot.

The conceptual account of retained source is stronger than the static image can prove. A gap can support that reading but cannot communicate storage or privacy guarantees. Product copy must explain source retention and independently selected local or cloud providers; the logo should stay modest about what it signifies.

The initial minimum current thickness is too dependent on a large drawing. At 24 pixels, narrowing can produce a weak filament and make the two halves feel unrelated. The exit face and the narrowest connecting region need explicit minimum dimensions, followed by actual raster inspection.

The l customization could read as a bar inserted into Mluva, especially if its upper flag disappears. Preserve enough conventional lowercase structure to read the name instantly, and avoid repeating caret motifs in every letter. The wordmark must survive as text before it earns recognition as artwork.

JetBrains Mono plus a narrowed l already belongs to the existing identity. That alone would be a minor restyling. The final wordmark needs a coherent additional relationship between the l's upright, the u's asymmetrical turn and the a's terminal while keeping those changes restrained.

This verbal proposal cannot establish distinctiveness against every existing software identity. The final pair still needs side-by-side visual review for generic wave-and-cursor associations, especially at 24 pixels. A successful explanation does not substitute for a recognizable silhouette.
revision:
The revised mark becomes a compact pair with an overall width only slightly greater than its height. Use a 24-unit construction field: the caret occupies x 19.25 to 22.25 and y 3 to 21; the voice occupies approximately x 1.75 to 16.25 and y 6.75 to 19.25. This gives the body a firm three-unit transparent interval from the receiver, an eighteen-unit caret height and enough surrounding air for rasterization. These are design proportions, not a pixel-perfect validation claim.

Replace the initial extended current with one broad, unbroken voiced body. Its lower left portion is generous and integrated into the whole shape, never a separate round head. The top contour rises gradually into an upper right shoulder; the lower contour scoops upward more firmly. Both meet a flat vertical delivery edge at x 16.25, extending from y 6.75 to 12.75. Keep every connection at least four units thick. The six-unit delivery face is substantial enough to feel like material arriving, while its parallel relationship with the caret makes the editing destination specific. Eliminate secondary crests, concave decorative nicks, trailing wisps and pointed ends.

Make the caret a filled three-unit-wide rectangle with barely softened corners, no more than 0.3 units in radius. It has no horizontal serifs. The rounded origin and squared receiver now differ through geometry, while sharing optical weight. Keep the body and caret disconnected. Judge the total pair by its visual center rather than placing the heavier body on a mathematically centered axis. The receiver remains still and calm; the source has already supplied the movement.

The final wordmark keeps exact Mluva spelling and the JetBrains Mono Medium foundation. Give the narrowed l a short but visible leftward upper flag and a rightward baseline foot roughly three quarters of one stem width long. Keep its stem uncompromisingly vertical. Let the u echo the body's broad lower turn with a modest optical fullness on the left, then return to a straighter right stem. Preserve the two-storey a, enlarge its counter only enough to keep it open, and square its finishing stem. Retain a conventional M and v, correcting dark joins without decorative cuts. Optical spacing supplies one continuous reading rhythm. The final artwork prompts below describe this revised treatment only; the initial wider arrangement and softer caret are not generation targets.
logoPrompt:
Create ONE final standalone logo symbol for Mluva, an open-source dictation and rewriting app for Omarchy. This is the CURRENT TO CURSOR study: a short substantial voiced current arriving beside a quiet upright editing caret. Logo symbol ONLY. Do not render Mluva, the concept title, letters, labels or any other text. Produce an actual transparent-alpha PNG with every background pixel transparent, not a white background and not a pictured checkerboard. Use only fully opaque monochrome near-black ink #171B22 for the artwork, with normal edge antialiasing. Center a generous-sized mark with clear transparent margins.

Draw precisely TWO disconnected solid filled shapes. The composition is compact, slightly wider than tall, with a low generous organic mass on the left and a tall plain upright on the right. On an imagined 24-unit field, the left mass spans x 1.75–16.25 and y 6.75–19.25. Its lower left body is broad and substantial, integrated smoothly into the whole form. Its top contour rises in one slow movement to an upper right shoulder. Its lower contour scoops upward more decisively to the same blunt delivery face. The right end is a straight vertical edge from y 6.75 to 12.75 at x 16.25. This flat face is crucial. Maintain a broad connection at least four units thick everywhere. Use only one flowing movement, no oscillating humps, no isolated round head and no thin neck. The impression is compact spoken material reaching a precise place to edit.

The right shape is a filled vertical caret rectangle from x 19.25 to 22.25 and y 3 to 21, three units wide and eighteen tall. Its corners are almost square, with at most 0.3-unit softening. No serifs. Leave the full three-unit transparent gap between the current's flat end and the upright. The caret reaches above and below the voiced body. Keep both shapes visually substantial at 24 pixels. Preserve asymmetry and warmth on the left, exact vertical stillness on the right.

Flat two-dimensional brand artwork, controlled smooth curves, filled silhouettes. No strokes, outlines, line art, speech bubble, microphone, waveform bars, abstract sine-wave icon, musical note, play arrow, chevron, terminal prompt, underscore, additional caret, sparkles, gradient, glow, shadow, bevel, texture, 3D, app tile, enclosing container, background, watermark, mockup or copied brand geometry. Do not fuse the two shapes. Do not add explanatory imagery.
wordmarkPrompt:
Create ONE final custom wordmark reading exactly Mluva, with uppercase M and lowercase l u v a, in that order. Wordmark ONLY. No logo symbol and no extra letters, caret, pipe, punctuation, underscore, caption or tagline. Produce an actual transparent-alpha PNG: transparent background pixels, not white and not a drawn checkerboard. Use only fully opaque monochrome near-black ink #171B22, with normal edge antialiasing. Give the single word comfortable transparent margins.

Use JetBrains Mono Medium letterforms as the recognizable starting point, then sculpt the five filled letter shapes into a calm, precise and distinctive software wordmark. Keep an unmistakable conventional capital M, open lowercase u, clear v and two-storey a. Retain the technical clarity of monospaced type while making the word optically spaced and compact. This is custom outlined lettering rendered as solid fills, never outline-only text.

Make lowercase l the primary signature: narrow its advance and shape around a steady vertical stem that recalls an editing caret while still reading instantly as lowercase l. Keep a short visible leftward flag at the top and a modest rightward foot at the baseline, about three quarters of a stem width long. Nearly square terminals, no pill shape. Make the u's lower left turn gently fuller than its right return, echoing a generous spoken current settling into precise editable text. Keep the change subtle and typographic, without a wave cutout. The right stem of u stays straight. Open the a's counter slightly for small-size clarity and give its finishing stem a clean square end. Preserve the M's normal internal diagonals and the v's recognizable shape, optically relieving only heavy joins.

Fit the spacing around the narrow l so the word reads continuously, without a large blank monospaced cell. Balance u–v and v–a by eye. Use consistent apparent weight and a steady baseline; do not connect the letters. Flat two-dimensional solid lettering only. No detached symbol, decorative cursor, ligature, stencil cuts, distressed effects, italics, rounded bubble lettering, arbitrary futuristic cuts, gradient, glow, shadow, texture, bevel, 3D, background panel, app tile, watermark, labels, mockup or copied brand treatment. Exact readable Mluva is the first requirement.
smallSizeRisks: At 24 pixels across, the transparent separation must remain visibly open; an antialiased near-touch would turn the composition into an ambiguous fused glyph.
The voice body's narrowest region must survive as a solid mass. If it becomes a thin stem, musical-note and sperm-like readings become more likely.
A caret rendered with fully rounded ends loses the deliberate editing character. Preserve almost square ends when preparing a small optical master.
The left body carries more area, so mathematical centering may make the pair feel left-heavy. Assess the total silhouette inside real 24-pixel launcher and header bounds.

The wordmark is not a five-letter launcher icon. Review it separately at practical reading widths, with special attention to the l flag and the a counter; use the symbol alone where those details cannot remain readable.
These are geometry targets for the study. Recognition and raster legibility require generated artwork and a real 24-pixel inspection before adopting the concept.
opticalRules: Keep exactly two solid filled shapes in the symbol and preserve their separation; use no strokes or outlines.
Final 24-unit target: caret x 19.25–22.25, y 3–21; voiced body approximately x 1.75–16.25, y 6.75–19.25.
Keep a three-unit gap from the current's flat delivery face to the caret and a minimum four-unit thickness through the voiced body.
Make the delivery face six units tall and exactly parallel to the caret. It should be the body's only emphatic straight edge.
Use a single rising movement with uneven upper and lower curvature. Do not add repeat crests, a separate bead, a thin tail or a pointed arrow tip.
The caret is three units wide with an eighteen-unit height; corner radius is at most 0.3 units. No crossbars or horizontal serifs.
Balance by apparent mass in the intended viewport. Preserve the low left origin and the upper right arrival; do not rotate or mirror the symbol.
In the wordmark, preserve exact Mluva spelling, a two-storey a and an identifiable lowercase l. Customization lives mainly in the l, the u's lower turn, the a terminal and optical spacing.
Keep a visible top flag and a short baseline foot on l. Do not add a trailing caret to the wordmark or convert its letters into a rebus.
Use one full-opacity ink per artwork. Prepare the inverse light fill from the same silhouette for dark surfaces; keep the surrounding alpha genuinely transparent.
motionRelationship: The mark shares the video's calm movement toward useful text. In a title reveal, the voiced body can settle from a slightly fuller low shape into its final rising contour while the caret remains fixed. Keep the change short and local; the final silhouette should hold long enough to become familiar. A faintly perceptible expansion of the voice body could relate to the existing 3.4-second breathing cadence, but the caret should not wobble, pulse or perform an attention-seeking blink. For a transition into the application, use a cut or restrained crossfade to real editable text; do not imply that all recognition instantly becomes a completed rewrite. The licensed water footage stays behind the film composition, never inside the transparent logo. Reduced motion uses the fully formed static pair. This is a study relationship, not a proposal to change the production recorder's status behavior.
